defs: ML system
All software, data and infrastructure around one or more models.
Model-centric view
Improve algorithms, features, hyperparameters for accuracy.
System-centric view
Improve data, infrastructure, deployment and UX for real-world reliability.
Hidden technical debt
Most of an ML system is glue code and infrastructure around a small ML core.
Core vs auxiliary ML
ML is the product (transcription) vs an add-on (audit-risk score).
EDDA
Experiment-driven data development running alongside the SE process.
Generative AI
Foundation-model system generating artefacts from natural instructions.
Agentic AI
Pursues complex goals with limited supervision via reasoning, planning and tools.
Cloud-native
Containers, service meshes, microservices, immutable infrastructure, declarative APIs.
Process maturity model
CMM-like scale for how well a team develops and manages ML.
confused: Generates an answer vs pursues a goal with actions.
Train once vs monitor and retrain.
Moderate, general hardware vs extreme, specialised, elastic.
recall.minute: Moving a research model to production exposes noisy data, latency and cost limits, product work, fragile pipelines, team gaps and fairness problems. The ML model is a component; the ML system includes UI, data collection, storage, serving, logging and monitoring, so system-centric thinking matters as much as model-centric tuning. Production pipelines add monitoring, data selection and regular updates, and hidden technical debt means the ML code is a small fraction of the whole. ML may be core (transcription) or auxiliary (audit-risk scoring), and large systems contain many ML components. An experiment-driven data track runs alongside the software track, and systems thinking asks how the system handles ML mistakes. Predictive, generative and agentic AI differ in purpose and infrastructure; cloud-native platforms host them. Case studies show 28 interacting models in autonomous driving and a nine-stage, feedback-heavy workflow with SE practices adapted for ML.
